subject: NorthByte: replacement vs. matchup — packaging and concession scenarios
messages:
From: Eleanor Zhang <eleanor.zhang@northbyte.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 Mar 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reconciling CloudQuill offer vs Redwood — can you map scenarios?

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to get a clear side-by-side: CloudQuill sent a commercial they say is non-negotiable, but the economics there look different depending on how we count inference vs. feature usage. Can you send: 1) a short comparison of packaging (seat vs. consumption) and 2) two concession scenarios if Redwood were to match the dollar figures (one conservative, one aggressive)?

I've attached CloudQuill's PDF quote and their runtime SLA excerpt. Our key constraints: 
- 12-month committed term preferred
- 99.9% latency SLA for inference in our US region
- Looking to keep TCO within current run-rate + 10% for year 1

If you can share a one-page workbook and a proposed legal/DocuSign cadence, that would help expedite procurement.

Best,
Eleanor
Eleanor Zhang
Head of ML Infrastructure
NorthByte

Attachment: competitor_quote.pdf (PDF, 220KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Eleanor Zhang <eleanor.zhang@northbyte.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 Mar 2028 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reconciling CloudQuill offer vs Redwood — can you map scenarios?

Eleanor — thanks for the note and the quote. Quick read-through here and attaching a short workbook and a draft pricing memo (attached) that lays out two paths we typically use when customers request a parity conversation. High level:

Option A — Price-match (conservative)
- We match the headline $/GPU-hour equivalence in their quote for year 1.
- Implementation: 6-week integration pilot.
- Commercials: 6 months of pilot credits (token-based) + 8% list discount across consumption for 12 months.
- Eligibility: needs a 12-month commit or prepaid credit block.

Option B — Transition package (aggressive)
- We offer an up-front migration credit to offset migration effort (one-time) + 10% usage discount for 12 months + reduced onboarding fees.
- Add-on: 60k tokens/month free for month 1–3 to validate latency/KPIs.
- SLA: We can commit to 99.9% regional latency SLO with a service credit schedule.

Key trade-offs I called out in the workbook: latency sensitivity (model family + sequence length), KV cache requirements, and egress patterns (NorthByte has heavy embedding use). We also included a quick runtime delta tab that compares expected token cost under both packaging models (seat/flat vs consumption-first).

Next steps:
- Eleanor: can you confirm the usage mix (prompt tokens vs embeddings by %)? The workbook assumes 70/30 split.
- Procurement: if price-match is preferred, we'll prepare a parity addendum + DocuSign path; if transition package is selected, we'll propose a migration credit SOW.

I've looped in Ben and Jonas to sign off on the concession matrix and DocuSign cadence.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Account Director — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: northbyte_proposal_v3.pdf (proposal, 180KB); runtime-comparison.xlsx (workbook, 120KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Eleanor Zhang <eleanor.zhang@northbyte.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 Mar 2028 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reconciling CloudQuill offer vs Redwood — can you map scenarios?

Kimberly / Eleanor — quick add from pricing:

We recommend a structured concession ladder rather than a single headline match. Practical example (for internal reference):
- Tier 1 (Committed, 12mo): match headline effective $/token; offer 1x migration credit (up to $40k) for onboarding tasks.
- Tier 2 (Committed, 24mo): deeper discount (12%) + extended SLA (99.95% uptime window for core inference endpoints); waive premium support fee for 6 months.
- Trade-in clause: if NorthByte migrates within 90 days and exceeds baseline throughput, we provide a retroactive implementation credit.

Negotiation notes:
- Avoid broad language 'price match' across all SKUs — define which models/workloads are eligible (we typically exclude very large-batch pretraining).
- Keep migration credit tied to milestones (pilot completion, production handoff) to limit risk.

Operational ask for procurement: please provide the opponent's renewal date and any auto-renewal windows so legal can space our DocuSign counter-offer accordingly. Also, I dropped a HubSpot deal note (see link) with proposed line items and a suggested discount schedule.

Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference

Related: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Eleanor Zhang <eleanor.zhang@northbyte.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 Mar 2028 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reconciling CloudQuill offer vs Redwood — can you map scenarios?

Eleanor — thanks for the clarity. After reviewing the workbook and Ben's ladder, engineering ops and I validated that the latency SLO (99.9%) is attainable for your workload on our Standard inference profile assuming the cached-KV pattern you described. A couple of concrete commitments if NorthByte signs a 12-month consumption commitment by April 15: 

- We will provide an onboarding/migration credit of up to $35k (applies to professional services hours or partner integrator invoices).
- For months 1–3: 60k free tokens/month and accelerated support (SLA-backed response targets).
- Pricing: match CloudQuill's effective token price for the primary model family used in your workloads (we'll exclude custom large-batch training).

Next steps to close quickly:
1) Eleanor: confirm usage mix (prompt vs embeddings) and the competitor renewal date.
2) Kimberly/Ben: I will draft the parity addendum + milestone-based SOW for the migration credit; legal to review standard carveouts.
3) Procurement: if everything looks good, we'll issue a DocuSign package with the addendum + main contract link; target signature window: Apr 5–15.

Quoted for context:
> On Fri, 24 Mar 2028 at 13:45 Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > Key trade-offs I called out in the workbook: latency sensitivity (model family + sequence length), KV cache requirements, and egress patterns (NorthByte has heavy embedding use).
>
Thanks — Jonas Weber
Head of Field Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: parity_addendum_draft.docx (draft, 45KB)
